anomalies.observed: The GND1 and GND2 pins of both isolated CAN transceivers (U10, U11) are connected to the same GND net.
anomalies.expected: GND1 and GND2 should be on separate isolated grounds (e.g., GND and GND_ISO) to maintain galvanic isolation between the logic side and the CAN bus side.

evidence.quote: GND [High Power] : ... U10.4(GND1,power_in) U10.5(GND2,power_in) ... U11.4(GND1,power_in) U11.5(GND2,power_in)
two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion)

anomalies.impact: The galvanic isolation of the CAN buses is completely defeated, allowing ground loops and removing protection between the CM4 and the motor controllers.

anomalies.observed: R60 connects D30.2 (cathode of the second LED in the dual LED D30) to ESTOP_OUT instead of GND. The net Net-(D30-K2) has no other connection to ground.
anomalies.expected: R60 should connect D30.2 to GND to complete the current path for the e-stop status LED.

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)

anomalies.impact: The e-stop status LED (second LED of D30) never lights because there is no return path to ground.

anomalies.observed: The VP pins of the TPD4E1U06 ESD protection devices U4 and U23 are left unconnected.
anomalies.expected: VP should be connected to a positive supply (e.g., +3V3) to provide proper ESD clamping for the Ethernet lines.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet lines have reduced ESD protection, making the board more susceptible to damage from electrostatic discharge.

parsed.summary: The design files contain multiple anomalies: the isolated CAN transceivers have their isolated grounds tied together, defeating isolation; the e-stop status LED D30 has a miswired current-limiting resistor R60; and the ESD protection devices U4/U23 have their VP pins left unconnected.
